page_map.boundary_note: Main text ends with Acknowledgments on physical page 9. References occupy pages 10–14, while Appendix A begins in the lower half of page 14 and continues through page 22.

abstract_sentences.text: Recent studies have investigated attention dynamics in large vision language models (LVLMs), yet existing methods remain limited in reliably distinguishing hallucinated from correct outputs, primarily because they rely solely on forward-pass attention and ignore gradient-based signals that reveal how token influence propagates through the model.

evidence.anchor: limited in reliably distinguishing hallucinated from correct outputs

abstract_sentences.text: To bridge this gap, we introduce LVLMs-Saliency, a gradient-aware diagnostic tool that quantifies the grounding strength of each output token by fusing attention weights with their gradients.

evidence.anchor: fusing attention weights with their gradients

abstract_sentences.text: Through analysis, we identify a decisive pattern: hallucinations occur when prior output tokens show low saliency to the next token prediction, indicating a failure of contextual memory.

evidence.anchor: Hallucinations occur when prior output tokens shows low saliency

abstract_sentences.text: Building on this insight, we propose a dual-mechanism inference-time framework: Saliency-Guided Rejection Sampling (SGRS) rejects low-saliency candidates before commitment, while Local Coherence Reinforcement (LocoRE) strengthens attention from the current token to its most recent outputs.

evidence.anchor: rejecting those with saliency below a context-adaptive threshold

abstract_sentences.text: Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly reduces hallucinations across multiple LVLMs, offering a robust and interpretable solution to improve model reliability.

evidence.anchor: significantly reduces hallucinations across multiple LVLMs

abstract_sentences.text: The code can be accessed in https://https://github.com/zhangbaijin/LVLMs-Saliency.

evidence.anchor: The code can be accessed

final_judgment.single_storyline: Autoregressive LVLM hallucination is framed as a loss of saliency from the next token to recent output context. LVLMs-Saliency measures the signal, SGRS gates candidate commitment, and LocoRE reinforces the next forward pass.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps Pattern 1, Eq. (1)–(10), Algorithms 1–2, benchmark/model setup, Tables 1–3, Figure 3 and the α latency trade-off. These pieces are sufficient to follow the intended diagnostic-to-intervention chain.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: The appendix contains Eq. (11), extra maps, fusion alternatives, efficiency, video results, ethics, reproducibility, token-level statistics, saliency decay, a high-saliency failure and layer/long-sequence checks. The move shortens the body but makes causal, compute and generality boundaries less visible.
final_judgment.best_pattern: The strongest writing pattern is a repeated token example carried from Figure 1/2 to Eq. (4)–(7) and then to the Figure 3 intervention, with Table 2 providing cross-model breadth and Table 3 exposing high-β degradation.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The largest gap is the jump from association plus an under-specified saliency-scaling intervention to a direct causal-link claim. The β=1.2 recommendation conflicts with Table 3 and Appendix C, while the principal counterexample and compute limits are delayed to the appendix.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For each mechanism claim, pair an observable token-level signal with a controlled intervention, explicit denominator and uncertainty, and a main-body failure case. Keep the algorithm defaults, table values and reproducibility statement numerically aligned.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule fits autoregressive LVLM decoding with an identifiable intermediate signal. It does not establish correctness when visual information is insufficient, context is ambiguous or the model is confidently wrong; backward-pass diagnostics also carry scale and latency limits.
final_judgment.theory_status: No theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, proof or formal complexity guarantee appears. The theory module is the saliency definition chain and its mechanistic interpretation.
final_judgment.layout_status: The PDF has 9 main pages, 5 reference pages and 9 appendix pages with page 14 shared by references and Appendix A. Most prose is single-column width; Algorithm 1/2 and several figures/tables are compact multi-column or full-width floats.
